dialogues.situation: Your order arrived wrong. Getting it fixed without a fight.

lines.en: Excuse me, I'm afraid there's a problem with my order.
lines.mn: Уучлаарай, миний захиалгад асуудал гарсан бололтой.

lines.en: Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. What happened?
lines.mn: Өө, уучлаарай. Юу болсон бэ?

lines.en: I ordered the chicken soup, but this is beef. And the bill charges for both.
lines.mn: Би тахианы шөл захиалсан ч энэ үхрийн мах байна. Тооцоонд хоёуланг нь бичсэн байна.

lines.en: You're right, that's our mistake. I'll bring the correct dish and fix the bill.
lines.mn: Таны зөв, бидний алдаа байна. Зөв хоолыг авчирч, тооцоог засъя.

lines.en: Thanks, I appreciate it.
lines.mn: Баярлалаа, талархаж байна.

lines.en: And the dessert is on us today.
lines.mn: Өнөөдөр амттанг манайх үнэгүй өгье.

key_phrases.note: 'I'm afraid' = complaint airbag. It softens whatever follows.

key_phrases.en: I ordered X, but this is Y
key_phrases.note: Fact, fact — no anger needed. Facts win complaints.
Warmer than 'thanks' — perfect after someone fixes a mistake.

practice.situation: Your soup is wrong. Open the complaint how?

options.text: Excuse me, I'm afraid there's a problem with my order.
options.why: Soft opener → cooperative waiter. English complaints start apologetically.

options.text: This is wrong food! Change it!
options.why: Wins the argument, loses the room. Bare commands read as aggression.
The most common learner choice — and the only truly wrong one.

lines.en: Did you get up to anything at the weekend?
lines.mn: Амралтын өдрөөр юу хийв?

lines.en: Not much — I went hiking with my cousin. We've been doing it every month lately.
lines.mn: Онц юмгүй — үеэлтэйгээ ууланд явлаа. Сүүлийн үед сар болгон явж байгаа.

lines.en: Nice! Whereabouts?
lines.mn: Гоё! Хаагуур?

lines.en: Near the river, about an hour out. You should come along next time.
lines.mn: Голын ойролцоо, нэг цаг орчим зайтай. Дараагийн удаад та ирээрэй.

lines.en: I'd love to. I've been meaning to get outdoors more.
lines.mn: Дуртайяа. Гадаа илүү их гарах гэж бодож л явдаг юм.

lines.en: It's a deal, then. I'll text you the date.
lines.mn: Тэгвэл тохирлоо. Өдрийг нь мессежээр хэлье.

key_phrases.en: Did you get up to anything at the weekend?
key_phrases.note: How natives really ask — not 'What did you do?'
= …хийе гэж бодож явдаг. Perfect continuous for a long intention.
The friendly invitation — 'come along' = хамт ирэх.

practice.situation: Someone invites you hiking and you want to go. Best reply?

options.text: I'd love to. When were you thinking?
options.why: Enthusiasm + a practical question — the accepting formula.
Grammatical but flat — 'I'd love to' carries the warmth.

options.text: Maybe, if I am not busy or tired or something.
options.why: Three escape doors in one sentence reads as 'no'.

dialogues.title_en: Giving your opinion in a discussion
dialogues.situation: Disagreeing with the room — and being thanked for it.

lines.en: So we're all agreed the app should launch next month?
lines.mn: Тэгэхээр бид бүгд аппыг ирэх сард нээхээр санал нэгдэж байна уу?

lines.en: Broadly, yes — though I'd push back on one point, if I may.
lines.mn: Ерөнхийдөө тийм — гэхдээ нэг зүйл дээр эсэргүүцэл хэлье, зөвшөөрвөл.

lines.en: Go ahead.
lines.mn: Хэлээрэй.

lines.en: From where I stand, the testing window looks optimistic. I'd sooner slip two weeks than launch with known bugs.
lines.mn: Миний харж байгаагаар тестийн хугацаа өөдрөг харагдаж байна. Мэдэгдэж буй алдаатай нээснээс хоёр долоо хоног хойшлуулсан нь дээр.

lines.en: That's a fair challenge. What would the two weeks buy us, concretely?
lines.mn: Зөв шүүмж байна. Хоёр долоо хоног бидэнд яг юу өгөх вэ?

lines.en: A full regression pass and a margin for surprises. I'd rather be boring than sorry.
lines.mn: Бүрэн давтан шалгалт, гэнэтийн зүйлийн нөөц. Харамсахаар бол уйтгартай нь дээр.

key_phrases.en: I'd push back on one point
key_phrases.note: C1 disagreement: technical, impersonal, no 'you are wrong'.
Frames opinion as perspective — leaves room for other views.
= Y гэснээс X нь дээр. Elegant preference structure.

practice.situation: The room agrees; you don't. Open with?

options.text: Broadly yes — though I'd push back on one point, if I may.
options.why: Agree first, then one precise challenge — dissent that gets heard.
Even if true, the room stops listening at word three.
The meeting is where opinions count — corridors change nothing.

dialogues.situation: The Q&A — where presentations are won or lost (guide §II).

lines.en: …and that brings me to the end. I'm happy to take questions.
lines.mn: …ингээд төгсгөлд хүрлээ. Асуултаа асууна уу.

lines.en: Thanks. Your growth figures — how sensitive are they to the exchange rate?
lines.mn: Баярлалаа. Таны өсөлтийн тоо — ханшийн өөрчлөлтөд хэр мэдрэмтгий вэ?

lines.en: Good question. Moderately — a ten percent swing moves the forecast by roughly three points. The details are in the appendix.
lines.mn: Сайн асуулт. Дунд зэрэг — арван хувийн хэлбэлзэл таамаглалыг гурван пункт орчим хөдөлгөнө. Дэлгэрэнгүй нь хавсралтад бий.

lines.en: And if I could follow up — what's the biggest risk you see?
lines.mn: Үргэлжлүүлж асуухад — таны харж буй хамгийн том эрсдэл юу вэ?

lines.en: Honestly? Hiring speed. The model assumes we staff up by June, and that's the assumption I'd watch.
lines.mn: Үнэнээр хэлэхэд? Хүн авах хурд. Загвар зургадугаар сар гэхэд бүрэн бүрэлдэхүүнтэй болно гэж үзсэн — энэ таамаглалыг л ажиглах хэрэгтэй.

lines.en: Appreciate the straight answer.
lines.mn: Шулуухан хариултад баярлалаа.

key_phrases.en: That brings me to the end
key_phrases.note: The standard landing phrase — signals Q&A cleanly.

key_phrases.en: Good question. / If I could follow up…
key_phrases.note: Q&A rituals: buy a second to think, extend politely.
Naming your own weak point builds more trust than hiding it.

practice.situation: You're asked something you can't fully answer. Best move?

options.text: Good question — I don't have the exact figure here, but I'll send it to you today.
options.why: Honesty + a concrete follow-up beats bluffing every time.
One caught bluff and the whole presentation is doubted.
Dodging is visible — the room remembers the question you skipped.

dialogues.situation: Telling a client the deadline will slip — keeping the relationship.

lines.en: Thanks for making time. I wanted to talk to you before you saw it in the report.
lines.mn: Цаг гаргасанд баярлалаа. Тайланд гарахаас өмнө өөрөө хэлье гэж бодсон.

lines.en: That sounds ominous.
lines.mn: Сонсоход л муу юм болсон бололтой.

lines.en: There's no way to dress it up: we're going to miss the March deadline. Realistically we're looking at late April.
lines.mn: Яаж ч чимэглэх аргагүй: бид гуравдугаар сарын хугацааг алдана. Бодитоор дөрөвдүгээр сарын сүүл гэж харж байна.

lines.en: That's a serious slip. What happened?
lines.mn: Ноцтой хоцролт байна шүү. Юу болсон бэ?

lines.en: Two suppliers failed us, and I'll own our part: we spotted it later than we should have. Here's what we're doing about it — and what I can offer you in return.
lines.mn: Хоёр нийлүүлэгч бидэнд гологдол өгсөн, мөн өөрсдийн бурууг хүлээе: бид байх ёстойгоос оройтож мэдсэн. Одоо ингэж засаж байна — хариуд нь танд үүнийг санал болгож чадна.

lines.en: I don't love the news, but I'll take the honesty. Walk me through the new plan.
lines.mn: Мэдээ нь таалагдахгүй ч үнэнч байдлыг нь үнэлье. Шинэ төлөвлөгөөг тайлбарлаж өгөөч.

key_phrases.en: There's no way to dress it up
key_phrases.note: Announcing directness — paradoxically, the politest way to deliver bad news.
'Own' a mistake = responsibility language that saves relationships.

key_phrases.en: Here's what we're doing about it
key_phrases.note: Bad news must arrive WITH the plan — never alone.

practice.situation: You must tell a client about a delay. Structure?

options.text: Warn them personally, state it plainly, own your part, bring the fix.
options.why: The four-step bad-news formula — honesty plus a plan.

options.text: Let them find it in the monthly report.
options.why: Discovered bad news costs double the trust of delivered bad news.
Even where true, pure blame reads as evasion — own your slice.

dialogues.situation: British-style indirectness — what the words are NOT saying.

lines.en: So — what did you make of my proposal?
lines.mn: За — миний саналыг юу гэж бодов?

lines.en: It's certainly… ambitious. There are some quite interesting ideas in there.
lines.mn: Лавтай яахав… том санаа юм. Дотор нь нэлээд сонирхолтой санаанууд байна.

lines.en: You hate it.
lines.mn: Танд таалагдаагүй байна шүү дээ.

lines.en: I wouldn't go that far. Let's say the budget section might benefit from another pass.
lines.mn: Тэгтлээ хэлэхгүй ээ. Төсвийн хэсэг дахин нэг нягтлахад гэмгүй гэж хэлье дээ.

lines.en: Meaning the numbers don't add up.
lines.mn: Өөрөөр хэлбэл тоо нийлэхгүй байна гэсэн үг.

lines.en: Meaning I'd love to see version two. With, perhaps, slightly braver honesty about the costs.
lines.mn: Өөрөөр хэлбэл хоёр дахь хувилбарыг харахыг хүсэж байна. Магадгүй зардлын талаар арай зоригтой үнэнч байдалтайгаар.

key_phrases.note: ⚠ In British English these often mean the OPPOSITE — praise this faint is criticism.
= it needs rework. The conditional hides the verdict.
Soft disagreement with your interpretation — while confirming half of it.

practice.situation: A British colleague calls your plan 'quite interesting, certainly ambitious'. They mean…?

options.text: They have serious doubts and expect a revision.
options.why: Faint praise + 'ambitious' is classic coded criticism — ask what to improve.

options.text: They love it and will approve it.
options.why: If they loved it you'd hear 'brilliant, let's do it' — enthusiasm is never this quiet.
The wording is too careful for inattention — coded language IS the message.

dialogues.situation: The classic questions — and answers that sound confident, not memorized.

lines.en: Thanks for coming in. Tell me a little about yourself.
lines.mn: Хүрэлцэн ирсэнд баярлалаа. Өөрийнхөө тухай товч ярина уу.

lines.en: Sure. I've worked in customer service for five years, mostly leading small teams.
lines.mn: Тэгье. Би таван жил үйлчилгээний салбарт ажилласан, гол нь жижиг баг ахалж байсан.

lines.en: What would you say is your biggest strength?
lines.mn: Таны хамгийн том давуу тал юу гэж хэлэх вэ?

lines.en: I'd say staying calm under pressure — last year we handled a system failure without losing a single client.
lines.mn: Дарамтад тайван байдаг гэж хэлнэ — өнгөрсөн жил системийн доголдлыг нэг ч үйлчлүүлэгч алдалгүй давсан.

lines.en: And why are you leaving your current job?
lines.mn: Одоогийн ажлаасаа яагаад гарч байгаа вэ?

lines.en: I've learned a lot there, but I'm looking for more responsibility, and this role offers exactly that.
lines.mn: Тэндээс их зүйл сурсан ч илүү хариуцлагатай ажил хайж байгаа — энэ албан тушаал яг тийм боломж юм.

key_phrases.note: Softens any self-praise: 'I'd say my strength is…' — confident but not arrogant.

key_phrases.en: I've worked in … for five years
key_phrases.note: Present perfect + for/since — the interview tense (experience touching today).
The polite reason for leaving — never criticise the old employer.

practice.situation: Interviewer asks why you left your last job. Best answer?

options.text: I've learned a lot, but I'm looking for a new challenge.
options.why: Positive about the past + forward-looking. The formula interviewers expect.

options.text: My boss was terrible and the salary was small.
options.why: Criticising a past employer is the classic interview mistake in any culture.

options.text: I don't know. I just want money.
options.why: Honest, maybe — but it answers a different question than the one asked.

dialogues.situation: Softening techniques (guide §JJ): disagree without a single hard 'no'.

lines.en: For this volume, the best we can do is 5,000 a month.
lines.mn: Энэ хэмжээнд сарын 5,000 бол бидний өгч чадах хамгийн сайн үнэ.

lines.en: I see. To be honest, that's a little higher than we had in mind.
lines.mn: Ойлголоо. Үнэнийг хэлэхэд, энэ бидний бодож байснаас арай өндөр байна.

lines.en: What figure were you thinking of?
lines.mn: Та ямар тоо бодож байсан бэ?

lines.en: Somewhere around 4,000. Would you be open to that if we signed for a full year?
lines.mn: 4,000 орчим. Бүтэн жилээр гэрээ хийвэл та үүнийг хүлээж авах уу?

lines.en: With a yearly contract… we might be able to meet you in the middle. Say 4,500?
lines.mn: Жилийн гэрээтэй бол... дундуур нь тохирч магадгүй. 4,500 гэвэл?

lines.en: That could work. Let me confirm with my team and get back to you tomorrow.
lines.mn: Болох байх. Багтайгаа зөвшилцөөд маргааш эргэж холбогдъё.

key_phrases.en: a little higher than we had in mind
key_phrases.note: 'A little' + comparative = polite disagreement. Never 'too expensive!'
Softest way to propose — a question, not a demand.
= дундуур нь тохирох. The compromise idiom of every negotiation.

practice.situation: Their price is too high for you. Best response?

options.text: To be honest, that's a little higher than we had in mind.
options.why: Softened disagreement keeps the negotiation alive — English hides the 'no'.
Bare commands burn the relationship — politeness lives in the phrasing.
Accepting the first price is not negotiating — and 'Would you be open to…?' costs nothing.

lines.en: Hi! Are you ready to order?
lines.mn: Сайн уу! Захиалахад бэлэн үү?

lines.en: Almost — what do you recommend?
lines.mn: Бараг — та юу санал болгох вэ?

lines.en: The beef noodles are really popular.
lines.mn: Үхрийн махтай гоймон их эрэлттэй.

lines.en: I'll have that, please. And a green tea.
lines.mn: Тэгвэл түүнийг авъя. Бас ногоон цай.

lines.en: Anything else?
lines.mn: Өөр юм авах уу?

lines.en: No, that's all, thanks. Could we get the bill after?
lines.mn: Үгүй, боллоо, баярлалаа. Дараа нь тооцоог авчирч өгөхгүй юу?

key_phrases.note: The friendliest question in any restaurant.
The set phrase for ordering — not 'I want' and not 'give me'.
= Тооцоо авах. Also common: 'the check' (US).

options.why: 'I'll have… please' is exactly how everyone orders.
Grammatical but blunt — 'I want' loses the politeness та carried.
Not an English structure.

talk.situation: Two colleagues meet in the morning.
talk.cue_mn: Өглөөний мэнд, Болд оо! Сайн уу?
talk.prompt: Morning, Bold! _____
talk.note: Answer is short: 'Good, thanks. And you?' — nobody gives a real report.

talk.situation: Two colleagues meet in the morning.
talk.cue_mn: Гайгүй ээ. Өнөөдөр завгүй юу?
talk.prompt: _____. Busy day today?
talk.note: = сайн байна. Very common, friendly.

talk.situation: Two colleagues meet in the morning.
talk.cue_mn: Уулзъя!
talk.note: Casual goodbye between people who meet often.

talk.situation: A colleague says: 'Morning! How are you?' — best reply?

options.why: Short + return the question — that is the whole game.

options.text: I am fine thank you and how are you my friend today.
options.why: Too long and formal — textbook English, not real life.
'How are you?' needs a feeling word, not yes/no.

talk.situation: First day with a new team member.
talk.cue_mn: Сайн уу Сара, би Болд. Санхүүгийн багийн нягтлан.
talk.prompt: Hi Sarah, I'm Bold. _____ in the finance team.
talk.note: am + an — the two words Mongolian drops. Never 'I accountant'.

talk.situation: First day with a new team member.
talk.cue_mn: Гурван жил орчим. Та? Ямар ажил хийдэг вэ?
talk.prompt: About three years. And you? _____
talk.note: = Ямар ажил хийдэг вэ? (NOT 'What is your job?' — this is the natural version)

talk.situation: First day with a new team member.
talk.cue_mn: Танилцахад таатай байна, Болд. Энд ажиллаад удаж байна уу?
talk.prompt: _____, Bold. How long have you been here?
talk.note: Say it once, at the first meeting only.

talk.situation: Someone asks: 'What do you do?' — best reply?

options.text: I'm an accountant. I work in finance.
options.why: Job + one detail. Perfect shape.
Missing 'an' — job words need an article.
'Things' says nothing — name the real job.

talk.situation: Buying water and asking the price.
talk.cue_mn: Уучлаарай, хийжүүлсэн ус байгаа юу?
talk.prompt: _____, do you have sparkling water?
talk.note: Opens ANY question to a stranger. Never start with the bare question.

talk.situation: Buying water and asking the price.
talk.cue_mn: Баярлалаа. Энэ ямар үнэтэй вэ?
talk.prompt: Thanks. _____ one?
talk.note: = Энэ ямар үнэтэй вэ?

talk.situation: Buying water and asking the price.
talk.cue_mn: Хоёрыг авъя. Картаар төлж болох уу?
talk.prompt: _____, please. Can I pay by card?
talk.note: 'I'll take…' is the natural buying phrase — not 'I want two'.

talk.situation: You want to know the price. Best question?

options.text: Excuse me, how much is this?
options.why: Excuse me + the set phrase.

options.text: What is the money of this?
options.why: Word-for-word translation — this phrase doesn't exist.
A bare command sounds rude in English (politeness lives in the phrasing).

talk.situation: Finding a pharmacy in an unfamiliar part of town.
talk.cue_mn: Уучлаарай, энд ойрхон эмийн сан байгаа юу?
talk.prompt: Excuse me, _____ pharmacy near here?
talk.note: THERE IS = байна. The question form for finding anything.

talk.situation: Finding a pharmacy in an unfamiliar part of town.
talk.cue_mn: Байгаа — чигээрээ яваад, банкан дээр зүүн тийш эргэ.
talk.prompt: Yes — go straight, then _____ at the bank.
talk.note: зүүн / баруун тийш эргэх

talk.situation: Finding a pharmacy in an unfamiliar part of town.
talk.cue_mn: Үгүй, явганаар таван минут орчим. Баруун гар талд, кафений хажууд.
talk.prompt: No, about five minutes on foot. It's _____, next to a café.
talk.note: ON for sides: on the right, on the left.

talk.situation: You repeat the directions to check you understood. Best way?

options.text: So — straight, then left at the bank?
options.why: Repeating back short is exactly what natives do to confirm.
Saying you understood ≠ checking you understood.
One-word commands sound rude — use 'Sorry, could you say that again?'

talk.situation: A bad line. THE most important skill for real conversations.
talk.cue_mn: Уучлаарай, дахин хэлж өгөхгүй юу? Холбоо муу байна.
talk.prompt: _____ The line is bad.
talk.answer: Sorry, could you say that again?
talk.note: Use it PROUDLY. Native speakers say it constantly too.

talk.situation: A bad line. THE most important skill for real conversations.
talk.cue_mn: Пүрэв, ойлголоо. Жаахан удаан ярьж болох уу? Англи хэл миний хоёр дахь хэл.
talk.prompt: Thursday, got it. _____, please? English is my second language.
talk.answer: Could you speak a little slower
talk.note: Nobody minds. It shows confidence, not weakness.

talk.situation: A bad line. THE most important skill for real conversations.
talk.cue_mn: Пүрэв, ойлголоо. Жаахан удаан ярьж болох уу? Англи хэл миний хоёр дахь хэл.
talk.prompt: Thursday, _____. Could you speak a little slower, please? English is my second language.
talk.note: = ойлголоо. Confirms you understood.

talk.situation: You didn't understand. Best response?

options.text: Sorry, could you say that again?
options.why: The single most useful sentence in spoken English.
Guessing builds wrong information — asking builds trust.
'What?' alone sounds annoyed. Add sorry + could you.

talk.situation: Arranging to meet at the weekend.
talk.cue_mn: Хөөе, бямбад завтай юу?
talk.note: free = завтай. ON + day.

talk.situation: Arranging to meet at the weekend.
talk.cue_mn: Нэг цагт ямар вэ? Дараа нь алхаж болно.
talk.prompt: _____ We could walk after.
talk.note: 'How about…?' — the softest way to suggest anything.

talk.situation: Arranging to meet at the weekend.
talk.cue_mn: Болно. Ямар нэг зүйл гарвал мессеж бичье.
talk.prompt: Perfect. _____, I'll text you.
talk.note: = Ямар нэг зүйл гарвал… ('comes up', present — no 'will' after if!)

talk.situation: You want to suggest 2 pm. Best way?

options.why: Soft suggestion — leaves room for the other person.

options.text: We will meet at two o'clock.
options.why: A decision, not a suggestion — sounds like an order.

options.text: If you will be free at two, we meet.
options.why: No 'will' after 'if': if you're free at two…

talk.situation: A short project meeting; you need to update and disagree politely.
talk.cue_mn: Бүтэхгүй байж магадгүй — тоог шалгаж амжаагүй байж мэднэ. Аюулгүй талаас нь лхагва гэж тохирох уу?
talk.prompt: _____ — the numbers may not be checked. Could we say Wednesday to be safe?
talk.answer: I'm not sure that works, actually
talk.note: How natives say NO politely — never a bare 'No, impossible'.

talk.situation: A short project meeting; you need to update and disagree politely.
talk.cue_mn: Бүтэхгүй байж магадгүй — тоог шалгаж амжаагүй байж мэднэ. Аюулгүй талаас нь лхагва гэж тохирох уу?
talk.prompt: I'm not sure that works, actually — the numbers may not be checked. _____ to be safe?
talk.note: Suggesting a change as a question keeps everyone comfortable.

talk.situation: A short project meeting; you need to update and disagree politely.
talk.cue_mn: Зөв санал. Лхагва болгоё.
talk.prompt: _____. Wednesday it is.
talk.note: = Зөв юм байна. Accepting someone's argument gracefully.

talk.situation: You disagree with a date. Best way to say it?

options.text: I'm not sure that works — could we say Wednesday?
options.why: Soft no + alternative = professional disagreement.
Bare 'no' burns goodwill — English wraps disagreement in softeners.
Silence = agreement in meetings. Speak, softly.

talk.situation: A new friend asks about your family.
talk.cue_mn: Танд ах дүү бий юу?
talk.prompt: _____ brothers or sisters?
talk.note: The A1 question machine: Do you have brothers? Do you have time?

talk.situation: A new friend asks about your family.
talk.cue_mn: Ганц эгчтэй. Тэр Дарханд амьдардаг.
talk.prompt: Just one sister. _____ Darkhan.
talk.note: he/she + livES — the -s that Mongolian never asks for.

talk.situation: A new friend asks about your family.
talk.cue_mn: Тийм, нэг ах, хоёр эгч дүү. Та?
talk.prompt: Yes, one brother and two sisters. _____
talk.note: Two words that keep every conversation alive.

talk.situation: Someone asks: 'Do you have brothers or sisters?' Best reply?

options.why: Answer + return the question — conversation is ping-pong.
One word ends the game. Add a detail and 'And you?'

options.text: My family is a difficult and long story from history.
options.why: Too much for small talk — keep A1 answers light.

talk.situation: Describing a simple illness.
talk.cue_mn: Хоолой өвдөж, толгой өвдөж байна. Хоёр хоногийн өмнө эхэлсэн.
talk.prompt: _____ and a headache. It started two days ago.
talk.note: Illness = I HAVE + a + body problem. Never 'my throat is pain'.

talk.situation: Describing a simple illness.
talk.cue_mn: Хоолой өвдөж, толгой өвдөж байна. Хоёр хоногийн өмнө эхэлсэн.
talk.prompt: I have a sore throat and a headache. _____.
talk.note: ago = өмнө; the past-simple marker doctors always ask for.

talk.situation: Describing a simple illness.
talk.cue_mn: Ханиад шиг байна. Амарч, бүлээн юм ууж, үүнийг өдөрт хоёр удаа ууна уу.
talk.prompt: It looks like a cold. Rest, warm drinks, and take this _____.
talk.note: once / twice / three times a day — өдөрт нэг/хоёр/гурван удаа.

talk.situation: The doctor asks what's wrong. Best answer?

options.text: I have a headache. It started yesterday.
options.why: Symptom + when it started — exactly what a doctor needs.
'Pain' is a noun: I have a pain / my head hurts / I have a headache.
'Sick of' means annoyed, not ill! Say 'I feel sick.'

talk.situation: Getting across town with a talkative driver.
talk.cue_mn: Төв номын сан руу. Хэр удах вэ?
talk.prompt: The central library, please. _____
talk.note: TAKE = хугацаа зарцуулах: It takes 20 minutes.

talk.situation: Getting across town with a talkative driver.
talk.cue_mn: Зүгээр. Гол хаалган дээр буулгаж өгөхгүй юу?
talk.prompt: No problem. _____ the main entrance?
talk.note: drop me at = буулгаж өгөх. Polite request shape again.

talk.situation: Getting across town with a talkative driver.
talk.cue_mn: Тэгье. Ирлээ — найман мянга болно.
talk.prompt: Sure. Here we are — _____.
talk.note: How sellers say the price — 'that will be…'

talk.situation: You want to know the journey time. Best question?

options.why: The fixed phrase with TAKE for time.
Time here is uncountable, and the verb is TAKE: how long will it take?
Needs do-support and 'arrive': When do we arrive?

talk.situation: Your order arrived wrong. Getting it fixed without a fight.
talk.cue_mn: Уучлаарай, миний захиалгад асуудал гарсан бололтой.
talk.prompt: Excuse me, _____ with my order.
talk.note: 'I'm afraid' = complaint airbag. It softens whatever follows.

talk.situation: Your order arrived wrong. Getting it fixed without a fight.
talk.cue_mn: Баярлалаа, талархаж байна.
talk.prompt: Thanks, _____.
talk.note: Warmer than 'thanks' — perfect after someone fixes a mistake.

talk.situation: Your soup is wrong. Open the complaint how?

options.text: Excuse me, I'm afraid there's a problem with my order.
options.why: Soft opener → cooperative waiter. English complaints start apologetically.

options.text: This is wrong food! Change it!
options.why: Wins the argument, loses the room. Bare commands read as aggression.
The most common learner choice — and the only truly wrong one.

talk.situation: Small talk that builds friendships.
talk.cue_mn: Амралтын өдрөөр юу хийв?
talk.answer: Did you get up to anything at the weekend?
talk.note: How natives really ask — not 'What did you do?'

talk.situation: Small talk that builds friendships.
talk.cue_mn: Дуртайяа. Гадаа илүү их гарах гэж бодож л явдаг юм.
talk.prompt: I'd love to. _____ get outdoors more.
talk.note: = …хийе гэж бодож явдаг. Perfect continuous for a long intention.

talk.situation: Small talk that builds friendships.
talk.cue_mn: Голын ойролцоо, нэг цаг орчим зайтай. Дараагийн удаад та ирээрэй.
talk.prompt: Near the river, about an hour out. _____ next time.
talk.note: The friendly invitation — 'come along' = хамт ирэх.

talk.situation: Someone invites you hiking and you want to go. Best reply?

options.text: I'd love to. When were you thinking?
options.why: Enthusiasm + a practical question — the accepting formula.
Grammatical but flat — 'I'd love to' carries the warmth.

options.text: Maybe, if I am not busy or tired or something.
options.why: Three escape doors in one sentence reads as 'no'.

talk.situation: Disagreeing with the room — and being thanked for it.
talk.cue_mn: Ерөнхийдөө тийм — гэхдээ нэг зүйл дээр эсэргүүцэл хэлье, зөвшөөрвөл.
talk.prompt: Broadly, yes — though _____, if I may.
talk.answer: I'd push back on one point
talk.note: C1 disagreement: technical, impersonal, no 'you are wrong'.

talk.situation: Disagreeing with the room — and being thanked for it.
talk.cue_mn: Миний харж байгаагаар тестийн хугацаа өөдрөг харагдаж байна. Мэдэгдэж буй алдаатай нээснээс хоёр долоо хоног хойшлуулсан нь дээр.
talk.prompt: _____, the testing window looks optimistic. I'd sooner slip two weeks than launch with known bugs.
talk.note: Frames opinion as perspective — leaves room for other views.

talk.situation: The room agrees; you don't. Open with?

options.text: Broadly yes — though I'd push back on one point, if I may.
options.why: Agree first, then one precise challenge — dissent that gets heard.
Even if true, the room stops listening at word three.
The meeting is where opinions count — corridors change nothing.

talk.situation: The Q&A — where presentations are won or lost (guide §II).
talk.cue_mn: …ингээд төгсгөлд хүрлээ. Асуултаа асууна уу.
talk.prompt: …and _____. I'm happy to take questions.
talk.answer: that brings me to the end
talk.note: The standard landing phrase — signals Q&A cleanly.

talk.situation: The Q&A — where presentations are won or lost (guide §II).
talk.cue_mn: Үргэлжлүүлж асуухад — таны харж буй хамгийн том эрсдэл юу вэ?
talk.prompt: And _____ — what's the biggest risk you see?
talk.note: Q&A rituals: buy a second to think, extend politely.

talk.situation: The Q&A — where presentations are won or lost (guide §II).
talk.cue_mn: Үнэнээр хэлэхэд? Хүн авах хурд. Загвар зургадугаар сар гэхэд бүрэн бүрэлдэхүүнтэй болно гэж үзсэн — энэ таамаглалыг л ажиглах хэрэгтэй.
talk.prompt: Honestly? Hiring speed. The model assumes we staff up by June, and _____.
talk.note: Naming your own weak point builds more trust than hiding it.

talk.situation: You're asked something you can't fully answer. Best move?

options.text: Good question — I don't have the exact figure here, but I'll send it to you today.
options.why: Honesty + a concrete follow-up beats bluffing every time.
One caught bluff and the whole presentation is doubted.
Dodging is visible — the room remembers the question you skipped.

talk.situation: Telling a client the deadline will slip — keeping the relationship.
talk.cue_mn: Яаж ч чимэглэх аргагүй: бид гуравдугаар сарын хугацааг алдана. Бодитоор дөрөвдүгээр сарын сүүл гэж харж байна.
talk.prompt: _____: we're going to miss the March deadline. Realistically we're looking at late April.
talk.answer: There's no way to dress it up
talk.note: Announcing directness — paradoxically, the politest way to deliver bad news.

talk.situation: Telling a client the deadline will slip — keeping the relationship.
talk.cue_mn: Хоёр нийлүүлэгч бидэнд гологдол өгсөн, мөн өөрсдийн бурууг хүлээе: бид байх ёстойгоос оройтож мэдсэн. Одоо ингэж засаж байна — хариуд нь танд үүнийг санал болгож чадна.
talk.prompt: Two suppliers failed us, and _____: we spotted it later than we should have. Here's what we're doing about it — and what I can offer you in return.
talk.note: 'Own' a mistake = responsibility language that saves relationships.

talk.situation: Telling a client the deadline will slip — keeping the relationship.
talk.cue_mn: Хоёр нийлүүлэгч бидэнд гологдол өгсөн, мөн өөрсдийн бурууг хүлээе: бид байх ёстойгоос оройтож мэдсэн. Одоо ингэж засаж байна — хариуд нь танд үүнийг санал болгож чадна.
talk.prompt: Two suppliers failed us, and I'll own our part: we spotted it later than we should have. _____ — and what I can offer you in return.
talk.answer: Here's what we're doing about it
talk.note: Bad news must arrive WITH the plan — never alone.

talk.situation: You must tell a client about a delay. Structure?

options.text: Warn them personally, state it plainly, own your part, bring the fix.
options.why: The four-step bad-news formula — honesty plus a plan.

options.text: Let them find it in the monthly report.
options.why: Discovered bad news costs double the trust of delivered bad news.
Even where true, pure blame reads as evasion — own your slice.

talk.situation: British-style indirectness — what the words are NOT saying.
talk.cue_mn: Лавтай яахав… том санаа юм. Дотор нь нэлээд сонирхолтой санаанууд байна.
talk.prompt: It's certainly… ambitious. There are some _____ ideas in there.
talk.note: ⚠ In British English these often mean the OPPOSITE — praise this faint is criticism.

talk.situation: British-style indirectness — what the words are NOT saying.
talk.cue_mn: Тэгтлээ хэлэхгүй ээ. Төсвийн хэсэг дахин нэг нягтлахад гэмгүй гэж хэлье дээ.
talk.prompt: I wouldn't go that far. Let's say the budget section _____.
talk.note: = it needs rework. The conditional hides the verdict.

talk.situation: British-style indirectness — what the words are NOT saying.
talk.cue_mn: Тэгтлээ хэлэхгүй ээ. Төсвийн хэсэг дахин нэг нягтлахад гэмгүй гэж хэлье дээ.
talk.prompt: _____. Let's say the budget section might benefit from another pass.
talk.note: Soft disagreement with your interpretation — while confirming half of it.

talk.situation: A British colleague calls your plan 'quite interesting, certainly ambitious'. They mean…?

options.text: They have serious doubts and expect a revision.
options.why: Faint praise + 'ambitious' is classic coded criticism — ask what to improve.

options.text: They love it and will approve it.
options.why: If they loved it you'd hear 'brilliant, let's do it' — enthusiasm is never this quiet.
The wording is too careful for inattention — coded language IS the message.

talk.situation: The classic questions — and answers that sound confident, not memorized.
talk.cue_mn: Дарамтад тайван байдаг гэж хэлнэ — өнгөрсөн жил системийн доголдлыг нэг ч үйлчлүүлэгч алдалгүй давсан.
talk.prompt: _____ staying calm under pressure — last year we handled a system failure without losing a single client.
talk.note: Softens any self-praise: 'I'd say my strength is…' — confident but not arrogant.

talk.situation: The classic questions — and answers that sound confident, not memorized.
talk.cue_mn: Тэгье. Би таван жил үйлчилгээний салбарт ажилласан, гол нь жижиг баг ахалж байсан.
talk.prompt: Sure. _____ customer service for five years, mostly leading small teams.
talk.note: Present perfect + for/since — the interview tense (experience touching today).

talk.situation: The classic questions — and answers that sound confident, not memorized.
talk.cue_mn: Тэндээс их зүйл сурсан ч илүү хариуцлагатай ажил хайж байгаа — энэ албан тушаал яг тийм боломж юм.
talk.prompt: I've learned a lot there, but _____, and this role offers exactly that.
talk.note: The polite reason for leaving — never criticise the old employer.

talk.situation: Interviewer asks why you left your last job. Best answer?

options.text: I've learned a lot, but I'm looking for a new challenge.
options.why: Positive about the past + forward-looking. The formula interviewers expect.

options.text: My boss was terrible and the salary was small.
options.why: Criticising a past employer is the classic interview mistake in any culture.

options.text: I don't know. I just want money.
options.why: Honest, maybe — but it answers a different question than the one asked.

talk.situation: Softening techniques (guide §JJ): disagree without a single hard 'no'.
talk.cue_mn: Ойлголоо. Үнэнийг хэлэхэд, энэ бидний бодож байснаас арай өндөр байна.
talk.prompt: I see. To be honest, that's _____.
talk.answer: a little higher than we had in mind
talk.note: 'A little' + comparative = polite disagreement. Never 'too expensive!'

talk.situation: Softening techniques (guide §JJ): disagree without a single hard 'no'.
talk.cue_mn: 4,000 орчим. Бүтэн жилээр гэрээ хийвэл та үүнийг хүлээж авах уу?
talk.prompt: Somewhere around 4,000. _____ that if we signed for a full year?
talk.note: Softest way to propose — a question, not a demand.

talk.situation: Softening techniques (guide §JJ): disagree without a single hard 'no'.
talk.cue_mn: Жилийн гэрээтэй бол... дундуур нь тохирч магадгүй. 4,500 гэвэл?
talk.prompt: With a yearly contract… we might be able to _____. Say 4,500?
talk.note: = дундуур нь тохирох. The compromise idiom of every negotiation.

talk.situation: Their price is too high for you. Best response?

options.text: To be honest, that's a little higher than we had in mind.
options.why: Softened disagreement keeps the negotiation alive — English hides the 'no'.
Bare commands burn the relationship — politeness lives in the phrasing.
Accepting the first price is not negotiating — and 'Would you be open to…?' costs nothing.

talk.situation: Ordering food with a colleague.
talk.cue_mn: Бараг — та юу санал болгох вэ?
talk.prompt: Almost — _____
talk.note: The friendliest question in any restaurant.

talk.situation: Ordering food with a colleague.
talk.cue_mn: Тэгвэл түүнийг авъя. Бас ногоон цай.
talk.prompt: _____ that, please. And a green tea.
talk.note: The set phrase for ordering — not 'I want' and not 'give me'.

talk.situation: Ordering food with a colleague.
talk.cue_mn: Үгүй, боллоо, баярлалаа. Дараа нь тооцоог авчирч өгөхгүй юу?
talk.prompt: No, that's all, thanks. _____ after?
talk.note: = Тооцоо авах. Also common: 'the check' (US).

talk.situation: Ordering soup. Best sentence?

options.why: 'I'll have… please' is exactly how everyone orders.
Grammatical but blunt — 'I want' loses the politeness та carried.
Not an English structure.
